newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker after lackluster session.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker after lackluster session.

text.p: COMEX copper ended weaker Monday after a lackluster but stable session, leaving last week's sharp gains largely intact.
Canada and much of Europe was closed due to public holidays, dampening activity on LME with a knock on effect on COMEX, dealers said.
LME stocks fell 2,100 tonnes to 141,575 tonnes, continuing the strong downtrend.
"But the outflow was ignored and we ended slightly down," a dealer said.
July COMEX copper settled 0.35 cent weaker at 115.85 cents per pound, traded 117.20 to 115.50 cents. Spot May went out unchanged at 117.00 cents.
The LME cash to three months backwardation was $68/$72, slightly lower than Friday.
COMEX copper stocks dipped 386 short tons Monday to 39,606 short tons.
The market was still underpinned by potential labor disputes in Chile and falling LME stocks.
A spokesman for Kennecott Utah Copper said the planned smelter maintenance was within the timeframe envisioned.
The 270,000-tonne smelter was shut April 15 for 42 days.
